rules.title: Explicit columns, never SELECT *
rules.what: Query the columns the code actually uses; never SELECT * on tables that can grow.
rules.why: SELECT * transfers and deserialises every column, including the ones added later that the code never wanted: the cost grows with the schema, not with the need.
rules.how: Name columns in SELECT, projections in ORM (values(), only(), select()). Destructive for EXISTS-style probes is fine; document the exception.

patterns.note: SELECT * in SQL (string literals masked by the scanner in .sql files).

verify.how: Audit finds no unmasked SELECT * outside documented exceptions.

limits: Column lists must stay maintainable; an explicit exception comment beats a silent *.

rules.title: No N+1 query
rules.what: Accessing related data inside a loop over results (one query per row) is replaced by a join, a batched IN query or ORM eager loading.
rules.why: N+1 multiplies the query count by the row count: 1,000 rows become 1,001 queries, transferring the same connection and parsing overhead a thousand times.
rules.how: Fetch relations in one query (join, select_related, include, @ManyToOne with fetch batch), or batch by ids. Use the language rule for the ORM in play (rules/lang/*.json).

patterns.note: Loop over an ORM queryset; verify no lazy relation access inside the body.
Iteration over results; check for await-in-loop DB calls.

verify.how: Query-count assertion (Django assertNumQueries, test logger, or EXPLAIN count) on the collection endpoint is constant in the row count.

rules.title: Indexes aligned with access paths
rules.what: Index what the queries filter and sort on; remove indexes nothing uses. Prove index use with the query plan, not with hope.
rules.why: A missing index turns every lookup into a table scan that grows with the data; a useless index taxes every write for a read nobody makes.
rules.how: EXPLAIN the hot queries, add covering indexes for the filters and sorts, review index usage statistics at each ecodesign review.

verify.how: EXPLAIN output for the hot queries shows index usage; index usage stats show no dead index.

limits: Each index slows writes and takes space; they are trade-offs to record, not more-is-better.

rules.title: Pagination by cursor on large collections
rules.what: Large collections paginate with a cursor or a keyed range, not with OFFSET on growing tables.
rules.why: OFFSET 10000 makes the database walk the 10,000 rows before returning any: the cost grows linearly with the page number for a user who rarely passes page 3.
rules.how: Cursor (WHERE id > ? LIMIT n) or keyset pagination on a stable order; document the ordering contract.

patterns.note: Parameterised OFFSET pagination; candidate for keyset pagination on large tables.

verify.how: Latency of the last page is within the same budget as the first on a large fixture dataset.

limits: Small tables paginate fine with OFFSET; the rule targets collections that grow.

rules.title: Retention and deletion from day one
rules.what: Every table and store has a retention policy (what, how long, who decides) and a deletion or archival path that actually runs.
rules.why: Data kept 'just in case' is stored, backed up, replicated and audited forever. The cheapest storage optimisation is not keeping it.
rules.how: Declare retention per data class at schema design; implement TTL/cron jobs; verify they run; archive before deleting what may be legally retained.

verify.how: Schema review shows retention per table; deletion jobs have run logs.

limits: Legal retention overrides deletion and is recorded as an obligation, not an oversight.

rules.title: Right store for the data shape
rules.what: Store data in the store designed for its shape and access: blobs in object storage, sessions in a KV store, documents in a document store, not everything in the relational base by reflex.
rules.why: A blob in the database doubles the base's size, its backups and its memory for a workload it handles worst; the object store does it for a fraction and streams it.
rules.how: Classify data (relational, document, blob, ephemeral) and match the store; keep the migration cost in the decision.

patterns.note: Binary large object column; verify the size profile justifies DB storage over object storage.

verify.how: Storage inventory matches data classes; large-object sizes profiled.

limits: Small blobs (avatars under a cap) are fine in DB; the rule targets files by size and access profile.

rules.title: Parameterised queries, reused plans
rules.what: Queries go through parameters/prepared statements, not string concatenation of user input.
rules.why: String-built queries defeat plan caching (a parse per variation), are the textbook SQL injection vector, and make the database re-plan work it has already planned.
rules.how: Parameterised queries everywhere user input meets SQL; ORM query builders by default; literals only for constants.

patterns.note: SQL built by concatenation or interpolation (strings are masked by the scanner, so this matches the build pattern); REVIEW for injection and plan reuse.

verify.how: No user input reaches SQL outside parameters; SQL lint/injection tests pass.

limits: Security rule first; the resource argument backs it, not replaces it.

rules.title: Compact and archive at rest
rules.what: Compress what is large and repetitive at rest (logs, exports, cold data, JSON columns); archive cold data out of the hot base.
rules.why: Storage at rest costs space, backup, replication and energy for every copy. Large repetitive data compresses by an order of magnitude and nothing is lost.
rules.how: Compress exports and logs at write; partition old data out of the hot path; measure compression ratios and access latency before generalising.

verify.how: Storage footprint and backup duration measured before/after compression/archival.

limits: CPU cost of decompression on access; measure the read path, not just the write gain.

rules.title: One copy, one consistency boundary
rules.what: Do not persist the same derived or binary data in several places unless the trade-off is measured and documented; model data so that each fact has one owner.
rules.why: Every extra copy costs storage, backups and replication, and drifts out of sync; normalisation removes update anomalies, measured denormalisation removes repeated work.
rules.how: Normalise by default; denormalise or materialise only with a measured read benefit and an explicit refresh strategy; reference blobs instead of copying them.

verify.how: Each duplicated field or materialised view records its reason and refresh strategy.

rules.title: Bound NoSQL scans, indexes and item growth
rules.what: In NoSQL stores, model access patterns first, avoid full scans and fan-out reads on request paths, bound secondary indexes, and expire or archive items with TTLs.
rules.why: A scan reads every partition; an unbounded table and index set grow storage and write amplification forever.
rules.how: Query by partition key; paginate with continuation tokens; TTL on transient items; review each secondary index against a query.

patterns.note: Full scan or empty-filter query; candidate on request paths.

verify.how: Request-path queries use keys (no Scan); TTL configured on transient collections.
